pageCache.pageTitle: Level 3 Certificate in Core Maths - Poole Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Level 3 Certificate in Core Maths
Studying core maths will better prepare you for the mathematical demands of work, study and life. The course has been developed with employers, universities and professional bodies as valuable preparation for higher education and employment. Students will develop their mathematical modelling and problem-solving skills, their mathematical reasoning and their ability to analyse data to make decisions.
Course content
Core Maths develops the mathematical skills gained at GCSE. It focuses on using and applying maths to solve problems from other subjects, work and everyday life. There are three components to our course:
Probability and Risk
Statistics
Estimation
Finance and Percentages
Mathematical modelling
Normal Distribution
Exponentials
Regression to the mean
Business and risk
Randomised control trials
Fermi estimates
Medical screening
Making decisions with risk
Mean and standard deviation
Normal distribution
Problem solving cycle
Sampling methods
Spearman’s rank
Chi-squared hypothesis test
Entry requirements
This qualification is open to any student except those studying A-Level mathematics.
Assessment
Students sit two written papers at end of Year 13:Paper 1 (50%): Introduction to Quantitative Reasoning. 2 hrsPaper 2 (50%): Critical Maths or Statistical Problem Solving. 2 hrsStudents have a choice of which specification they follow from the two listed above, and this determines which Paper 2 they sit at the end of the course. All papers will have pre-release materials which will be available from the March before the exams. [Calculators are allowed in all exams.]

pageCache.pageTitle: Level 3 Award in Personal Finance - Poole Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Level 3 Award in Personal Finance
This is for students who want to develop their knowledge of handling their finances. It is a small qualification that focuses on aspects useful to independent adult life.
Students will learn about personal financial activity, financial planning and different types of financial products and services.
Entry requirements
This qualification is open to any student.
Assessment
Students will be assessed by way of a one-hour written exam which shall be taken in Year 12.

pageCache.pageTitle: A-level Further Mathematics - Poole Grammar School
pageCache.text:
A-level Further Mathematics
Further mathematics courses allow you to study beyond the A-level mathematics syllabus, covering topics that other students would only meet at university. It is a great choice if you love maths and have found GCSE easy. Please see A-level Mathematics for more information about the subject as a whole.
Course content
On top of your A-level maths studies, you will study:
Core Pure Mathematics 1
Core Pure Mathematics 2
Further Pure Mathematics 1
Further Mechanics 1
Entry requirements
GCSE grade 8 in mathematics. You must be studying A-level mathematics as one of your main three A-levels.
Assessment
Core Pure Mathematics 1 Exam (25%): 1hr 30 minsCore Pure Mathematics 2 Exam (25%): 1hr 30 minsFurther Pure Maths 1 Exam (25%): 1hr 30 minsFurther Mechanics 1 Exam (25%): 1hr 30 mins

pageCache.pageTitle: AS level Modern Foreign Languages - Poole Grammar School
pageCache.text:
AS level Modern Foreign Languages
Subject to capacity we sometimes offer AS French and Spanish. These are taught in the same classes as our A-levels in those subjects. AS students study the subject during Year 12 only, sitting their exams in May of that year. In Year 13 they continue to study their three main A-levels and gain some private study time. Please see A-levels in Modern Foreign Languages for more information about these subjects as a whole.
Entry requirements
GSCE grade 6 in the relevant foreign language.
Assessment
Paper 1 (45%): 1 hr 45 mins. Listening, Reading and Writing.Paper 2 (25%): 1 hr 30 mins. Translating from English, and writing on one text or film.Paper 3 (30%): About 15 minutes. Speaking.
Languages are consortium subjects, with teaching split between Poole Grammar School and Parkstone Grammar School.
